title: Secure DNS and Web Access Filtering System

sections.title: Purpose
paragraphs: This specification records the project purpose, stakeholder constraints and unresolved decisions stated in the source evidence below.
This SRS describes the software's required behavior for users, administrators and the Project Analyst reviewing the specification.

sections.title: Scope
paragraphs: Design a secure DNS and web-access filtering system for a university that protects students, faculty, staff, and administrative users from malicious or unauthorized internet destinations. The system should inspect DNS requests, block access to known malicious domains, apply different browsing policies based on user roles, and provide administrators with a dashboard for reviewing blocked requests and security events. Administrators should be able to create and update filtering policies, allow approved exceptions, investigate repeated attempts to access blocked resources, and temporarily restrict users when suspicious behavior is detected. The platform should maintain audit logs of policy changes and filtering decisions, integrate with centralized authentication, and support deployment across academic buildings, hostels, laboratories, and administrative offices. The solution should be secure, scalable, reliable, and manageable.

requirements.statement: The system shall implement a secure DNS and web-access filtering mechanism to protect all university users from malicious or unauthorized internet destinations.

The system shall inspect DNS requests, block access to known malicious domains, apply role-based browsing policies, and provide administrators with a dashboard for reviewing blocked requests and security events.

Administrators shall be able to create, update filtering policies, allow approved exceptions, investigate repeated access attempts to blocked resources, and temporarily restrict users when suspicious behavior is detected.
The solution shall be secure, scalable, reliable, and manageable.

The platform shall maintain audit logs of policy changes and filtering decisions, integrate with centralized authentication, and support deployment across academic buildings, hostels, laboratories, and administrative offices.
